summary.intent: Resolve a merge conflict on change #54 (PR #81, the held-out benchmark set) after PR #77 and #80 merged into main, and keep the Rust support PR stack moving.
summary.outcome: Merged main into the held-out branch, resolving the single conflict in scripts/rg-compare.py by keeping both sides. Raised the three recall gates to 0.9, updated help text, added decision-log entry 34, and committed the merge and ratchet after the harness and repo checks ran.

repo: Change numbers (e.g. #54) are not PR numbers; change 54 maps to PR #81 (the held-out set), so the number must be mapped to a branch first.

scripts/rg-compare.py is a conflict hotspot: PR #77 reworked it into a per-language `Lang` structure with shared TEST_DIRS and TS/Rust test suffixes mirroring `is_test_path`, and PR #81 adds a `HELD_OUT` marker.
Repo checks are run via `just ci`, plus `python3 -I scripts/rg-compare.py` after `cargo build --release`; typos is also run when appending decision-log entries.
Decisions are recorded as numbered sections in a decision log (entry 34 added this session).
Rust recall gate (`--min-rust-recall`) defaulted to 0 until Rust support landed; on main, Rust rows against fd measure 22/24 (identifiers 11/13, questions and members 11/11).
TS harness baseline is identifier 58/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16.

code.finding: Conflict resolved by keeping main's test-path constants together with the branch's HELD_OUT marker.

After the #77 merge it uses main's rayon fan-out and Candidate fold, with allow_tests kept in FileContext; retrieve_blocks keeps the test_blocks flow so per-file folding stays in walk order and diagnostics stay deterministic.
Gate defaults were changed from 0 to 0.9 and their help strings and header text were updated, since the help text said '0 until…'.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output without user authority, so verify PR mergeability and CI directly with gh before relaying status.
Distinguish agent-reported results from verified ones when summarizing, since CI on merge commit a9c8a8b was still pending.
After resolving conflicts, check that references from both sides still line up, then rebuild and rerun the full harness and `just ci` before committing.
A byte-for-byte comparison of old main against merged release binaries (stdout, stderr, exit code) is an effective regression check for a refactor that should not change TS behaviour.

friction: The merge of #77 conflicted in three files (Cargo.lock, pipeline/mod.rs, rg-compare.py), and #81 then conflicted again on rg-compare.py after #77 and #80 merged.
The user's reference 'change: #54' was ambiguous and needed a lookup to map it to PR #81.
Help strings and the header line still said '0 until…' after the gate defaults changed, requiring a second pass of fixes.
CI on #77's merge commit was still pending (1 passed, 7 pending), so it could not be called green.
open_items: Raise `--min-rust-recall` from 0 to the value main measures, with one-miss headroom, once #77 is merged and settled (the 0.9 gate ratchet was applied on the #81 branch).
Check the held-out and Rust rows together after #81 is in.
Entire Gates on #77, #79, #80, #81 and release PR #59 are waiting on the user's approval.
The bounded-work PRs start after the open PRs are approved.
No standalone `cargo test --doc` was run on the #77 merge.
Wait for GitHub CI on #77's merge commit a9c8a8b to finish.
